text: Compressing a file shrinks its size by removing redundancy, making it faster to store or send; anyone can reverse it. Encrypting scrambles the contents using a key so only authorized people can read them. Everyday uses: compressing photos into a ZIP file to email them, and encrypting your phone so thieves can't access your data.
task: Explain the difference between compressing a file and encrypting it, including one everyday use of each.
